Jr. NBA Rookie Practice 7 dokumentiert d: Jr. NBA Rookie Practice 7 documents the ‘2 on 2 Numbers Game’: two called players attack the ball; the team in possession plays offense and the other two defend for one possession. The source explicitly calls for active defense, footwork and shot contests. The task is therefore reliable as a game-like team-defense context, but not as specific help/recover instruction.
Jr. NBA beschreibt zwei Verteidiger in e: Jr. NBA describes two defenders in a continuous closeout/help sequence. The on-ball defender works as ‘ball’, while the other jumps to help position; after the pass, the next defender rotates. After the live signal, the situation is played 2v2. Players in help position must see both ball and their own opponent and communicate.
Jr. NBA startet mit zwei Offensivspieler: Jr. NBA starts with two offensive players on the perimeter and two defenders reacting to a pass with a closeout or help. It then immediately becomes 2v2. This format is especially valuable for S7 because team defense appears as a shared space-and-ball task, not only footwork.
Jr. NBA verbindet Closeout/Tracing mit e: Jr. NBA links closeout/tracing to a subsequent live 2v2. After the defender's closeout, the ball movement is tracked; a pass to the coach triggers the live situation, bringing together cut, drive and defensive reaction. The drill links S7, S2 and S4.
FIBA/WABC empfiehlt für junge Spieler 3x: FIBA/WABC recommends that young players experience 3x3 not only in the half court but also in transition. It explicitly names ‘Basket then Ball’, channeling the dribbler, help/passing-lane principles and wide running lanes. The database classifies this as a simplified small-sided-game card; the specific U10–U12 adaptation is editorial.
Jr. NBA lässt die Kinder Bewegungen zu b: Jr. NBA has children perform movements to named court lines and spaces; the patterns include forward/backward/lateral movement, skipping, high knees and quick feet. The editorial focus is the link between spatial orientation, response to verbal cues and rhythm changes. The source also allows players to choose their own movements.
Zwei Spieler teilen sich zwei Bälle. Ein: Two players share two balls. One player dribbles with one hand and catches a second ball passed by the partner with the other; then repeat on the opposite side. The source names a tennis ball and a dribbling move before the catch as progressions. This is a clear K5/K6 task, but it is at Jr. NBA MVP level and therefore is not classified as a U8/U10 foundation card.
Zwei Linien greifen gleichzeitig an. Der: Two lines attack simultaneously. At two cones, the ballhandler chooses between a baseline and middle drive; the second player reacts to the drive direction and runs either to the corner or the basket. This is more than a spacing demonstration: the ball decision creates the open space and the off-ball player reacts to it.
Zwei Angreifer spielen gegen einen Verte: Two attackers play against one defender in transition. Jr. NBA explicitly describes it as a fast-break decision and names 2v1 defense as a learning objective alongside the offensive decision. This closes the prior S6 gap at the application level.
Das offizielle Video demonstriert eine A: The official video demonstrates a task that makes passing, compared with dribbling, tangible as faster ball movement. For the model, it is primarily relevant as a link between passing, running and spatial ball movement. The editorial K6/S5 assignment goes beyond the original designation and is therefore marked as an editorial classification.

DBB Easybasket – Dreiergruppen bewegen s: DBB Easybasket – groups of three move with a dribbling child in the middle; signals trigger direction changes, stops or passing sequences.

Jr. NBA Starter beschreibt eine 5er-Grup: Jr. NBA Starter describes a group of five in which four players are active and one person waits at a defined rest/substitution station; three attackers play against one defender. This makes the drill particularly useful as a directly documented organization format for small groups. It can also be marked in the catalogue as a reference for ‘3 active + 1 defender + 1 rotation role’.
Eine komplexere Screenfolge wird vorgege: A more complex screen sequence is prescribed; 3v3 is then played live. Source: Jr. NBA MVP Practice 11. QA: A.
EX-130: Jr. NBA All-Star beschreibt eine: EX-130: Jr. NBA All-Star describes a 2v1 task that deliberately starts with poor initial spacing. Without dribbling, the attackers must create space through passing and movement; variations change space and opponent pressure. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/page/11/ . QA A.
EX-132: Jr. NBA All-Star „Partner Closeo: EX-132: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘Partner Closeout Shooting’ links a closeout with an immediate shoot/drive decision. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/page/8/ . QA A.
EX-133: Jr. NBA Starter „4 on 4 Continuo: EX-133: Jr. NBA Starter ‘4 on 4 Continuous with Constraints’ uses several competition rules such as a time bonus, defensive shutdown and changing basket direction. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/starter/page/3/ . QA A.
EX-134: Jr. NBA MVP „3 on 3 from Help th: EX-134: Jr. NBA MVP ‘3 on 3 from Help the Helper’ starts with drive, help and help-the-helper, followed by live 3v3. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/mvp/ . QA A.
EX-135: FIBA/WABC Level 1 „Two Halves Sc: EX-135: FIBA/WABC Level 1 ‘Two Halves Scrimmage’ allows the coach to alter rules deliberately so that specific offensive or defensive principles come to the fore. Source: https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/documents-corporate-wabc-coaching-level-manuals-level-1-eng.pdf . QA A.
EX-137: FIBA/WABC beschreibt Offensive R: EX-137: FIBA/WABC describes offensive rebounding as part of offense and recommends continuing activity after the shot until a score or defensive control. For the database, this is better captured as a cross-cutting rule than as one isolated drill. Source: https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/documents-corporate-wabc-coaching-level-manuals-level-1-eng.pdf . QA A/methodology.
Das DBB-Easybasket-Handbuch beschreibt z: The DBB Easybasket handbook describes two children with a ball passing to each other from about 3 m apart. One may start toward the basket at any time; the other reacts and follows. DBB names different pass types and varied passing distances as variations. The original description therefore directly includes adapting execution to distance.
Der DBB beschreibt an einer Station ausd: At one station, DBB explicitly states that the rhythm of the final two steps before shooting is important for a layup in motion. Children first practise the take-off rhythm, then receive a ball, stay in rhythm and finish. Obstacles and varied routes additionally create a transition from movement to ball action.
Der DBB-Jugend-Minileitfaden definiert a: The DBB youth mini guide explicitly defines internalizing the layup's two-step rhythm as the learning objective. The original task links dribbling, receiving a pass, two steps and take-off; the method initially permits a flexible left-right or right-left sequence and later adds a dribble before the two-step contact.
FIBA/WABC beschreibt eine konkrete Partn: FIBA/WABC describes a specific partner task with one ball each: one player dribbles forward and the other backward. On the coaching signal, both switch roles/direction; as a progression, the leading player may also choose sideways and the partner takes the opposite direction. For the model, this is K4 because the running/dribbling rhythm must be reorganized when the signal changes; K2/K3 are also directly involved.
Jr. NBA führt eine explizit so benannte: Jr. NBA includes an explicitly named rhythm-dribbling task at MVP level. It names rising/lowering, speed changes, several steps in one dribble and free movement variations. Because of the high curricular entry level, the card is documented as a later progression rather than a U8–U10 core card.
Jr. NBA All-Star beschreibt eine 1v1-Auf: Jr. NBA All-Star describes a 1v1 task without dribbling, using pivots to gain space, then adding one dribble as a technical progression. The defender applies real pressure; starting position and time limit can change the task tactically or competitively.
Die ersten Aktionen sind festgelegt (Pas: The first actions are prescribed (pass-and-cut or pass-and-ball-screen), then play becomes live 3v3. This directly transfers prescribed technical/tactical patterns into open decisions.
Die Offense beginnt mit fünf Pässen, dan: The offense begins with five passes, after which play becomes live. Documented progressions include scoring only from a screening action or only from drive-and-kick. This is a useful core for team defense, spacing and group decisions.
Drei offensive Spieler (Passer, Screener: Three offensive players (passer, screener, cutter) play screen/read actions in short bursts; 3v3 or numerical-advantage formats, different screen types and defensive adjustments are possible. The source names timing, spacing, communication and decision-making as objectives.
Zwei Spieler werden über gleiche Nummern: Players with matching numbers form teams; the coach puts the ball into play, two players attack it and the resulting 2v2 position is immediately played live. The source emphasizes active defense, footwork and contesting.
Ein 3v2-Fastbreak wird unmittelbar in ei: A 3v2 fast break immediately turns into a 2v1 going the other way. The current Jr. NBA description explicitly names spacing and good decisions in transition as learning objectives.
Drei Angreifer greifen zwei Verteidiger: Three attackers play against two defenders; after a shot/turnover, the opposite direction immediately begins with a new 3v2. Additional technical constraints are an outlet pass and a limit on number of passes.
Die Possession beginnt mit Baseline-Driv: The possession starts with a baseline drive; a help defender stops the ball and a third defender ‘helps the helper’; then play becomes live. This is a particularly clear team-defense and rotation card.
Die Mannschaften starten jede Possession: Teams start every possession with a pick-and-roll, after which play is free. The task thereby moves the pick-and-roll from a prescribed sequence into an open game problem.
Guard und Post spielen eine 2v2-Situatio: Guard and post play a 2v2 situation from the side ball screen; the coach may prescribe or vary the pick-and-roll defense.
Der Coach verändert seine Positionierung: The coach changes their positioning against the screen. The passing and screener decision depends on whether the defender drops or steps up aggressively; in the first case the pass goes to the shooter, in the latter to the slip.
Der Coach verteidigt den Screener unters: The coach defends the screener differently (hedge, drop or between the players), and the ballhandler must read the appropriate follow-up action/shooting decision.
Vier Verteidiger reagieren auf Ballbeweg: Four defenders react to ball movement, box out or pursue the rebound and then play live after an offensive rebound. The format challenges players to get five consecutive defensive rebounds in competition.

Jr. NBA verbindet Closeout/Tracing mit e: Jr. NBA links closeout/tracing to a subsequent live 2v2. After the defender's closeout, the ball movement is tracked; a pass to the coach triggers the live situation, bringing together cut, drive and defensive reaction. The drill therefore links S7, S2 and S4.

Das Spiel beginnt mit einem Elbow-Pass u: The game starts with an elbow pass and a prescribed cut/screen structure; it then becomes live 3v3.
EX-131: Jr. NBA All-Star „Chaos Reboundi: EX-131: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘Chaos Rebounding’ starts with an uncontested initial shot and moves into live 2v2/3v3. Shot-clock, dribble, pass, shot-location and scoring variations change the task. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/page/11/ . QA A.
EX-136: FIBA/WABC beschreibt beim On-Bal: EX-136: For the on-ball screen, FIBA/WABC describes several dribbler options: Turn the Corner, Split, Runner and Step Back, plus Slip, Roll and Pop/Flare by the screener. The specific task is therefore particularly suitable as a U14–U18 component for decision-making and pick-and-roll training. EX-138/139: Jr. NBA MVP nutzt diktierte: EX-138/139: Jr. NBA MVP uses prescribed 3v3 starts with a down screen or pick & roll before play becomes live. This format is especially valuable for transferring from a prescribed pattern to an open decision. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/mvp/page/11/ . QA A.
EX-140/141: Jr. NBA All-Star nutzt 3v3 N: EX-140/141: Jr. NBA All-Star uses 3v3 No Dribble and 3v3 Continuous. Both formats create high participation and can be varied through scoring, time and role rules. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/ . QA A.
EX-142: Jr. NBA All-Star „3-Person Pass,: EX-142: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘3-Person Pass, Cut and Replace’ links pass, cut, replace and the transition into live play. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/ . QA A.
EX-143/144: Jr. NBA Starter dokumentiert: EX-143/144: Jr. NBA Starter documents Decision 1 on 1 and 3 on 2 Advantage as clear decision-making formats. Sources: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/starter/ and https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/starter/page/12/ . QA A.
EX-145: Jr. NBA Rookie „Advantage Number: EX-145: Jr. NBA Rookie ‘Advantage Numbers Game’ combines a random start, numerical selection, a small offensive advantage and live play to a score/stop. The source explicitly names quick decisions and a slightly changed task start. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/rookie/page/2/ .
EX-146: Jr. NBA Starter „Decision 1 on 1: EX-146: Jr. NBA Starter ‘Decision 1 on 1’ creates a genuine 1v1 choice through different starting positions. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/starter/ .
EX-147: Jr. NBA Starter „3 On 2 Advantag: EX-147: Jr. NBA Starter ‘3 On 2 Advantage’ creates a numerical advantage and can be changed through cut rules and ball-holding time. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/starter/ .
EX-148: Jr. NBA All-Star „3 on 3 No Drib: EX-148: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘3 on 3 No Dribble Game’ forces the offense to make passing and movement decisions and includes a clear rule for off-ball screens. The source also specifies a 30-second clock and defensive scoring. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/ .
EX-149: Jr. NBA All-Star „11-Person Tran: EX-149: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘11-Person Transition Drill’ links a 3v2 advantage, rebound/turnover and an immediate transition in the other direction. An outlet pass and a limited number of passes can serve as technical constraints. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/page/7/ .
EX-150: Jr. NBA All-Star „5 on 1 Build U: EX-150: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘5 on 1 Build Up’ develops a numerical advantage step by step from 5v1 to 5v5 and allows variation in the defensive entry order and offensive alignment. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/page/8/ .
EX-151: Jr. NBA All-Star „Square Rebound: EX-151: Jr. NBA All-Star ‘Square Rebounding’ combines a rotation signal, box-out and subsequent live play. The source distinguishes interior and perimeter box-outs and transitions after a defensive rebound. QA A. Source: https://jr.nba.com/basketball-practice-plans/all-star/page/8/ .
EX-152: FIBA/WABC beschreibt eine 3v3-Ak: EX-152: FIBA/WABC describes a 3v3 activity with a low-post decision in which the post must choose between 1v1 and a pass after help information. The format is classified for U16–U18 as a complex decision-making/team-offense task. QA A. Source: https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/documents-corporate-wabc-coaching-manual-level-2-eng.pdf .
